title: Time-Resolved Edge Flux on the SU(3) Triangle: A Cooperative-Decay Graph Framework with Exact Bateman Solutions
abstract: Cooperative emission from three-level ensembles is conventionally diagnosed through the radiated intensity alone, which cannot say which channels carry the photons at each instant. We promote every transition of the cooperative-decay graph into a time-dependent edge flux and show that node-wise conservation of this flux is an exact restatement of the Pauli master equation. Suppose the graph carries a depth function that decreases by one along every edge. Then the total cooperative rate is the descent speed of the mean graph depth, and its energy-weighted form gives the radiated intensity as $I(t)=-\dd\langle E\rangle/\dd t$ for arbitrary level spacings. The same ordering triangularizes the generator. This delivers the relaxation spectrum from the state exit rates, together with a generalized Bateman closed form for every population on an arbitrary finite directed acyclic graph, in which all exit-rate degeneracies are absorbed into a polynomial-times-exponential recursion.
summary: This paper introduces a Time-Resolved Edge Flux (TREF) framework to analyze cooperative decay in quantum systems, moving beyond simple intensity measurements. By mapping the master equation onto a time-dependent flux network on an SU(3) graph, the authors derive exact identities relating total decay rates to graph depth descent. They provide a general, robust Bateman solution applicable to any finite DAG, even when decay rates coincide.
main_problem: To develop an edge-resolved description of cooperative emission dynamics, moving beyond diagnostics based solely on the total radiated intensity.
main_result: The framework establishes that local flux conservation is mathematically equivalent to the Pauli master equation, yielding generalized Bateman closed-form solutions for state populations on arbitrary Directed Acyclic Graphs (DAGs).
method: The authors introduce a Time-Resolved Edge Flux (TREF) framework, treating the decay graph as a time-dependent flow network, and utilize a depth function to triangularize the system generator.
model_or_system: The system models cooperative emission from three-level ensembles, specifically utilizing the SU(3) triangle topology, governed by the Pauli master equation.
key_observables: Time-Resolved Edge Flux ($\Phi_{nm}(q; t)$), Total Cooperative Rate ($R_{	ext{tot}}(t)$), Radiated Intensity ($I(t)$), and state populations $P_u(t)$.
important_parameters: Transition rates ($w_{nm}(q)$), level spacings, and the graph depth function ($\Phi_d$).
main_assumptions: The framework relies on the Born–Markov approximation and assumes the graph structure can be ordered by a depth function.
figures_summary: A table summarizes three dipole-allowed three-level topologies (Ladder, $\Lambda$, Vee) on the SU(3) lattice, detailing channels, depth, and absorbing sets.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the TREF framework on the SU(3) lattice, establishing flux conservation and depth-descent identities. It then develops the algebraic consequences, including spectral analysis and the general Bateman closed form for arbitrary DAGs.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, rigorous mathematical formalism for analyzing open quantum systems dynamics, offering an edge-resolved view of decay processes that is highly relevant to quantum optics and superradiance.
